programDecisions.decision: Every future stock or industry study reports (a) a funded, ex-ante beta-matched alpha (stock leg vs beta*ETF + (1-beta)*investable cash), (b) an industry-neutral selection term, and (c) the exposure term separately. Raw within-date-demeaned benchmark-relative return is no longer a sufficient primary estimand.
programDecisions.reason: Within-date demeaning removes the market intercept but not (beta_i - mean beta) * R_market, so any risk-related signal changes sign with market direction. This matches the D_UNSTABLE / region-sign-unstable classifications of lowvol and the C2 pattern (wins in 2014/2018/2022/2024 down years, loses in 2025/2026 up years; HAC beta 0.630).
programDecisions.industryLabelNote: KR PIT industry labels exist only for the Top120 v4 reconstruction (terminated names 0%); a current KSIC/GICS label is never back-applied as PIT. Industry-matched terms are therefore secondary and carry their classification limitation.

programDecisions.decision: Portfolio-level ETF-relative NAV records are monitoring and implementation evidence, never the primary proof of alpha. Primary evidence for a 6-12M mechanism is event-level or calendar-time cross-sectional precision, gated by an outcome-free MDE before any outcome is read.
programDecisions.reason: At tracking error 13% (C2 measured 12.99%) a 3pp/yr edge needs about 147 years for 80% power; at 5% about 22 years. A 4-year prospective P0-P5 record cannot separate realistic alphas from zero.

programDecisions.decision: Recommend the owner grant ONE narrowly scoped Phase D exception for information axes that no prior KR study ever read (capital-allocation decisions, supply contracts, insider open-market trades), run once as EXPLORATORY_DEVELOPMENT_ON_OUTCOME_EXPOSED_KR_HISTORY under a frozen preregistration and power gate, followed by mandatory prospective confirmation. No exception for any Atlas-106 / regional-31 / Phase C feature.
programDecisions.reason: Phase D closed re-mining of already-read features. A never-read event axis is not conditioned on by prior searches, while the period itself (2025-26 semiconductor regime) remains exposed and must be reported as a split.

programDecisions.decision: Build a KOSPI liquidity-qualified PIT universe (signal-date median traded value >= 1bn KRW) as the event-study universe; Top120 stays the reference for existing studies. Terminations are BOUNDED (worst plausible and last-observed) and a verdict must hold under both, never imputed.
programDecisions.reason: Under the stated assumptions every Top120-only event study is POWER_MARGINAL or NO_GO; the broader universe (about 2.6x names) is the single largest power lever. Small-capital principle (AGENTS v2.24) permits it with cost discipline.

programDecisions.decision: Market layer is a risk budget, not an alpha source. Stop new market-timing signal search; keep C0/C1 and B-H1 prospective recorders as risk-overlay evidence.

studies.layer: STOCK (S4 ownership & capital flows / S1 payout)
studies.mechanism: The firm is its best-informed trader. A buyback decision followed by cancellation is a costly payout signal; acquisition without cancellation in Korea often serves control (literature: Korean investors price cancellation, not acquisition, as payout). Issuance (rights offerings, CB/EB, treasury disposal) is the opposite signal; internationally the issuance effect is driven more by post-issuance weakness than post-buyback strength (McLean-Pontiff-Watanabe 2009, 41 countries).
studies.horizonFit: Long-run drift in the literature is measured over 1-4 years; H126 primary, H252 secondary.
studies.overlapWithExisting: J03 registered but never built; C11 realised share-count change (Phase C, NO_DEVELOPMENT_EVIDENCE) is months later and net of all causes. The primary hypothesis uses decision-date events only; C11 is a control.
studies.primaryHypothesis: H1: issuers with a receipt-dated buyback-and-cancellation decision (or cancellation decision) earn positive funded ex-ante-beta-matched abnormal return over H126 net of a self-financed round trip (primary); industry-matched where a PIT industry label exists (secondary, labelled).
secondaryHypotheses: dilution side: rights offering / CB / EB / treasury disposal decisions underperform (implemented long-only as exclusion from an ETF-weighted book)
studies.data: DART list.json (receipt-dated, 2013+) plus decision-document fields: shares to acquire as % of shares outstanding, purpose, period, trust vs direct, cancellation; amendments separated from originals; signal = next session close after receipt.
controls: prior 21-session return (buybacks follow drawdowns: reversal confound)
studies.measuredDensity: Top120 per-252-session window: buyback decision or trust median 20 issuers, >=5 on 147/155 anchors; cancellations median 5, concentrated 2024-26 (PR #316 kr-event-report-counts-v1)
studies.survivorshipCorporateActionRisk: terminations within window bounded both ways; merger/tender buybacks excluded by purpose field
studies.costTurnover: one round trip per event; sleeve turnover about 200%/yr at H126; cost from the common #317 tariff incl. dated KR sell tax

studies.layer: STOCK (S5 material disclosure) with mandatory industry neutralisation
studies.mechanism: 단일판매·공급계약 discloses dated, sized future revenue (contract amount vs latest revenue, duration). If the market prices the announcement day but under-weights revenue recognised over the contract life, earnings surprises arrive in the next 2-4 quarters: a 6-12M drift. Korean event studies report a significant announcement-day rise and next-day reversal, so the claim is specifically about LARGE contracts relative to revenue, not the average filing.
studies.horizonFit: Revenue recognition runs over quarters; H126 primary.
studies.overlapWithExisting: No feature set reads contract size. M3 backlog (US industry aggregate, #302) failed but is a different unit (industry macro series).
studies.primaryHypothesis: H2: contracts >= 10% of latest annual revenue (the disclosure-materiality line, frozen before outcomes, not searched) earn positive funded ex-ante-beta-matched abnormal H126 return net of costs (primary); industry-matched where a PIT label exists (secondary, mandatory to report).
